notes: belongs_to_language_group is transitive (RELATIONS.md). Families are disjoint: a firm GCI makes membership in Indo-European and in Uralic incompatible, so the edit takes Hungarian out of Uralic (via its old branch) and the old answer 'no' for Balto-Slavic follows. 'Magyar' is another name for Hungarian (a background equality, so Magyar is left out of distinct). related[0] (the language Hungarian is most closely related to) is read as the language that shares a group with Hungarian: Hungarian's groups followed by includes_language, with Polish's membership of Slavic (polish_slavic) and Finnish's of Uralic (finnish_uralic) firm background facts. q1 uses the chain tag of author_wrote_in: Petőfi wrote in Hungarian, so he wrote in every group Hungarian belongs to.
